title: Forgot your password? Reset it yourself
body: A quiet "Forgot password?" link now sits under the sign-in fields — on the web and in Settings → Cache cloud. Confirm your email and we send a reset link. It always says the same calm thing whether or not that email has an account, so it can't be used to find out who's registered. And it's honest about what a reset does: getting back into your account isn't the same as unlocking your data. If your cache is sealed just for you (zero-knowledge), the link gets you in, but your data still opens only with your recovery file or code — so the app says exactly that and points you there, instead of pretending your data is back. Accounts that keep a spare key with us just open as normal.

title: Your cache is yours — zero-knowledge by default
body: New accounts are now sealed so only you can open them — we can't read your data, by math, not policy. So you can't get locked out, every account gets a recovery file to save at setup (add a recovery code too if you like), and any one of them opens your cache. Prefer we keep a spare key to help you back in? That's now a clear opt-in checkbox, off by default. Manage all your unlock methods any time in Settings → Cache cloud. Existing accounts keep working exactly as before.

title: Connect your bank right from your phone
body: No computer needed. Paste your SimpleFIN setup token on the web and your cache pulls your balances and transactions itself, then syncs them to your other devices — all computed on your device, sealed so the cloud can't read it. SimpleFIN holds the bank login (we never see it) and the key stays on your phone (so we can't see your money either). Tap the new "How does this work?" for a plain walkthrough. Sync when you want; it always tells you how fresh your numbers are.

title: What changed finds you now
body: When something new ships, your cache tells you — a short "What's changed" note opens when you sign in, or right when an update lands if you're already here. It waits if you're mid-sentence, never shows the same thing twice, and everything is still in the bell whenever you want it.

title: A calmer dock, and a tidier profile
body: The cloud button moved into the dock and stopped resizing itself every time it synced — no more dock sliding around under your cursor. Your profile folds its activity into one line you can open in its own window, and account switching works from there. The Roadmap button is now an option you can turn on rather than a default.

title: Get your money in — right in the browser
body: The web app can now take money in on its own, no desktop required. Download a CSV from your bank and drop it onto your cache (or Menu → Import statement) — your browser builds your ledger and works out your spending, safe-to-spend and income, then syncs it to your devices, sealed so the cloud never sees it. Re-import as often as you like; duplicates are skipped.

title: News lands here now
body: Messages grew a second inbox: What's new. Every update we ship shows up here — quietly. A small mark on the bottom corner of the messages button means there's news; the top corner is still people. Nothing here ever interrupts you.
